summary: Train to assess AML/CFT risk, plan examinations, and track remediation using FATF-informed exercises. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Risk-based AML/CFT supervision training shows financial supervisors and examination teams how to direct oversight according to assessed risks. It covers institutional risk profiling, risk-ranked examination planning, testing customer due diligence and transaction-monitoring controls, documenting evidence-based findings, and tracking remediation, with FATF guidance informing proportionate supervisory decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess, examine, or oversee AML/CFT controls at financial institutions. It suits supervisors and experienced compliance professionals with working familiarity with AML/CFT responsibilities. This course is designed for: Central-bank AML/CFT supervisors prioritizing institution-level supervisory attention. Financial-intelligence-unit supervisors assessing reporting entities’ AML/CFT control weaknesses. AML/CFT examination officers testing customer due diligence and transaction-monitoring controls. Prudential examiners incorporating money-laundering risks into bank examination plans. Non-bank financial institution supervisors reviewing licensing and ongoing AML/CFT controls. AML/CFT supervisory risk analysts maintaining sector and institution risk profiles. Regulatory examination team leads allocating staff across risk-ranked examinations. AML compliance leaders preparing evidence and responses for supervisory examinations. Financial crime compliance officers coordinating remediation evidence with supervisors. Supervisory policy specialists translating FATF standards into examination procedures.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with AML/CFT controls, financial institution operations, or regulatory supervision is recommended. No programming is required. Bring experience with supervisory or compliance documents; spreadsheet familiarity is helpful for the risk-matrix exercises.
